newsitem.title: USA: Texaco to buy Monterey for $1.1 billion in stock.
newsitem.headline: Texaco to buy Monterey for $1.1 billion in stock.

text.p: Texaco Inc. has agreed to buy Monterey Resources Inc., a California oil and natural gas producer, for more than $1.1 billion in stock, the companies said Monday.

The nation's third largest oil company will exchange about $21 worth of its stock for each of Monterey's 54.8 million outstanding shares, worth $1.15 billion. In addition it will assume $285 million of Monterey debt.
Monterey Resources Inc. is an independent oil and gas producer with primary holdings in California's San Joaquin Valley.
Monterey's stock jumped $5.25 to $20.31 in consolidated morning New York Stock Exchange trading. Texaco rose was 94 cents to $110.94, also on the NYSE.

Texaco said the acquisition will add 385 million barrels of oil reserves to its U.S. asset base and increase its California production by 54,000 barrels a day, to 180,000 barrels a day, with the potential for additional increases in coming years.

"Gaining Monterey's valuable reserves and talented employees will further enhance Texaco's leadership position in the area of enhanced oil recovery and give us a clear competitive advantage in a region in which we already have significant production and reserves, Texaco Chairman Peter Bijur said.
